Seulement au cas où ce mode opératoire ne peut pas être utilisé vu que l’adjudicataire ne disposerait pas d’une adresse e-mail, le mode opératoire exceptionnel pourrait alors être appliqué. L’expéditeur en question devra veiller à recevoir effectivement un accusé de réception et devra le conserver. Le délai effectif de livraison ou d’exécution débute le jour qui suit le jour d’envoi de l’e-mail (sauf autre disposition prévue dans la lettre de commande). Cette durée, dérogatoire à la durée de droit commun de 4 années prévue par la réglementation, se justifie par la lourdeur des investissements qui devront être faits au début du marché pour l’installation du logiciel et la reprise des données. De plus un changement d’outil demande des adaptations (changements informatiques pour l’intégration avec d’autres outils, formation des utilisateurs, etc.) chez le Pouvoir Adjudicateur et chez les pouvoirs publics bénéficiaires. Programme Aim The purpose of this training programme is to design, develop and deliver a training programme that build people’s understanding of self-harm and the role it plays in the life of a person who self-harms. The programme will build the knowledge and confidence of the learner to have a conversation if they are concerned that someone may be self-harming. The training programme should provide people who access it with a sense of hope and reassurance that people can build healthier coping mechanisms. Programme Objectives The training programme is intended to: Increase understanding of what self-harm is. Increase understanding of the relationship between self-harm and suicide. Build skills and confidence to engage with a person and speak openly about self-harm. Challenge the stigma surrounding self-harm Increase awareness of available supports and services Stage 1: An introduction to the subject of self-harm – communicating the ‘why’ functions of self-harm through lived experience experts. EAST AFRICAN COMMUNITY

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

Project Name: Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (EARSPforR)

Project ID: P176371

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Development of Animated Video Content with Infographics, Data Visualizations and Voice-over Narration for EAC Online Statistics Learning Materials

Reference No.: TZ-EAC-564358-CS-CQS

1. BACKGROUND

The East African Community (EAC) Secretariat is implementing the EAC component of the Eastern Africa Regional Statistics Program-for-Results (EARSPforR), with financing from the World Bank. The Program seeks to strengthen the production, harmonization, dissemination, and use of quality economic and social statistics in Eastern Africa.

Under EARSPforR, the EAC Secretariat has developed online learning materials in fourteen priority statistical domains for use by Partner State institutions and other data users. Although technically sound, many of the materials are text-heavy an

. The videos will incorporate infographics, accurate data visualizations, professional voice-over narration, captions, and transcripts, and will be suitable for the EAC Learning Management System, websites, and mobile access.

The assignment will be completed within a maximum of ten weeks from contract commencement. The principal deliverables will include an inception report and production plan; scripts, storyboards, and visual style; a pilot video; a complete draft video package; and final master, LMS/mobile, caption, transcript, thumbnail, editable-source-file, asset/licence, and completion-report packages.

The detailed Terms of Reference for the assignment can be accessed at www.eac.int under Procurement/Consultancies.

2. QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

The EAC Secretariat now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the assignment.

SCOPE OF SERVICE The Contractor shall provide enterprise -grade mobile and data services to the U.S. Embassy Panama. The prices listed below shall include all labor, service, equipment, technical support, materials, insurance (see FAR 52.228 -4 and 52.228- 5), overhead, and profit. The Government will pay the Contractor on a monthly basis for routine services that have been satisfactorily performed. The Contractor shall ensure that all services are delivered with high availability, reliability, and performance consistent with commercial best practices for enterprise telecommunications services. The Contractor shall offer two different plans to fulfill the Government needs: Basic Plan. Pay per use for actual calls (local, local long distance, international long distance), incoming and outgoing roaming calls, incoming and outgoing local SMS, incoming and outgoing international SMS, incoming and outgoing roaming SMS. Unlimited Smart Phones & Tablets Plan. A flat monthly rate per cellphone line that includes unlimited: local data, local minutes on-net, local minutes off-net, national long-distance minutes,

reliable international voice connectivity on a 24 -hour basis to the United States, Latin America, Europe, and other international destinations where commercially available telecommunications services exist. International calling services shall support clear and reliable voice communications consistent with the best commercial practices for enterprise telecommunications services. INTERNATIONAL ROAMING The Contractor shall provide broad international roaming coverage for voice, SMS, and data services through commercially established roaming agreements with foreign mobile network operators. Emphasis shall be placed on roaming availability and service reliability throughout the Western Hemisphere. The Contractor shall support international roaming services compatible with 4G/LTE services, and/or 5G services (5G services where commercially available). The Contractor shall provide the COR with an updated list of current international roaming partners and supported roaming countries at least every six (6) months. The Contractor shall disclose any significant roaming restrictions, unsupported regions, or service limitations in its proposal. SMS MESSAGING The Contractor shall provide reliable SMS messaging services on a 24- hour basis, including domestic, inter

The Contractor shall provide dedicated account management and support personnel who are fluent in both English and Spanish. The Contractor shall provide a dedicated customer support email address for the U.S. Embassy Panama. This capability must allow operators to identify and prioritize interoperability issues and potential workarounds within a single system. • 3.1.3.2 Platform Issue Tracking: The software shall provide a mechanism to record and maintain a history of platform-specific issues (e.g., design, testing, operational) through their entire lifecycle. This information must be linked to the platform specification to enable automatic updates to existing analyses. • 3.1.3.3 Capabilities & Limitations Summary: The software shall be capable of generating a consolidated, high-level summary of a platform's TDL capabilities, including implemented TDLs, message baselines, equipment fits, and network capabilities (e.g., Link 22, JREAP). 3.1.4 Interoperability (IO) Evaluation: The software shall provide a robust module to conduct detailed, multi-platform IO evaluations. STATEMENT OF WORK C. 1. OVERVIEW/BACKGROUND. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. The Library of Congress (Library) requires a contractor to produce, maintain, and support the latest generation of Digital Talking Book Machine (DTBM) devices, known as the DA2 (DTBM model Digital Advanced version 2), which were originally launched June 18, 2025. The National Library Service for the Blind and Print Disabled (NLS) provides free books and magazines in audio and braille format to eligible U.S. residents and citizens living abroad. NLS’ enabling legislation was changed in 2016 (Public Law 114-219) to permit NLS to develop and distribute devices to be used for reading any format, including DAISY (Digital Accessible Information System). As part of these services and products offered, NLS loans free DTBMs for use in consuming NLS-produced audio materials. NLS-produced audio materials are distributed via NLS DTBM cartridges and data files online via Braille and Audio Reading Download (BARD) website in AMR-WB+, MPEG I/Layer 3 (MP3), RIFF WAV, and other audio formats.
